I reviewed Vittorio a year ago, giving it 4 stars. I am so used to restaurants starting off well and then going downhill that it is a pleasure to report that Vittorio has remained consistently good over time, and has even improved. The food is not as classy as some of the top restaurants that I have reviewed in Ho Chi Minh City, but we are always extremely satisfied with our meals here, and this is the restaurant that we most frequently revisit for that reason, and also because of its outstanding value.

When you ask a waiter or waitress if such and such a dish is good today, you always expect them to say 'yes'. You don't expect honesty. In Vittorio I asked this question one day with regards to the steak, and the reply was 'you can have it, but maybe you should choose something else today.' I like that. Another thing I like is the fact that the Vietnamese owner, who speaks a little English with an Italian accent, is sometimes the person who will take your motorcycle as you arrive. and park it for you. How many restaurant owners/managers would do that? Impressive.

Another thing I like is that you are always given bread and butter with your meal, and sometimes peanuts with your beer. On our last meal here, I had the pan-fried chicken breast, Milanese style, with French fries. Basically it was a kind of chicken schnitzel, and was served with half a lime. It was generously sized, hot and absolutely delicious. The salad is always excellent, the beer is always cold and cheap. In fact we have never had a bad dish, and the service is also always friendly and efficient. In my view it is the best restaurant (along with Babar's Kitchen) in the Bui Vien/Pham Ngu Lao area. 

I just hope that Vittorio stays the same, and does not try to smarten itself up and become a more chic and expensive place to eat in the future. I look forward to perhaps reviewing it again in a year's time. In the meantime, it merits 5 stars.
